correctness.rationale: The precise [2/2] end-step map has scalar values in (0,1] on the nonnegative spectrum, so completed-step diagonal entries are strictly positive. Its large-step expansion forces nonpositive off-diagonals of the Laplacian pseudoinverse; effective resistance gives the adjacent formula (1). Three retained inequalities yield a 3x3 diagonally symmetrizable irreducible Perron matrix whose spectral radius is 1 at four vertices and strictly greater than 1 at five or more, forcing the claimed upper order cutoff and unique four-edge ray. The three-vertex two inequalities force the exact closed weight-ratio interval. Explicit exact rational end-step numerators and positive denominators prove sufficiency for every real positive step; rational identities were checked by the standalone verifier extracted from this package. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Prior 1995, 1997 and 1998 group-inverse matrix theory covers or closely approaches the necessary inverse-sign obstruction; no novelty is claimed for that necessary sign classification or the four-vertex weighted-path example. Lóczi--Ketcheson (arXiv:1303.6651v1) treats general rational absolute-monotonicity and positivity radii but does not state an all-timestep weighted-path graph-heat classification. The exact if-and-only-if [2/2] Gauss end-step statement, including positive-rational sufficiency, is neither a logical consequence of group-inverse M-matrix signs alone nor identified in inspected primary literature, accessible prior records or source-alias searches. A full specialist priority check is still needed for inaccessible 1995 and 1998 work. An earlier unweighted complete-multipartite scalar-filter theorem already covers the two-vertex and equal-weight three-vertex positive special cases and an unweighted four-vertex counterexample; those subcases are not independently original. The full arbitrarily weighted path iff statement, including the unique positive four-vertex ray, is not implied by that unweighted theorem.
residual_risks: Earlier group-inverse characterizations may contain broader material not fully available in 1995/1998 sources; their established necessary implications are acknowledged.

value.rationale: A concrete graph-heat numerical invariant is classified over all real positive path weights and all graph orders: the safe set changes from an unrestricted two-node family to a closed 3-node ratio interval to a unique 4-node ray and disappears completely thereafter. The cutoff is not merely an isolated example or tautological sign test; it combines a dimension-independent obstruction with constructive finite rational certificates that establish a useful exactly identified unconditional positivity domain for a widely used A-stable fourth-order method.
